docs.contenu:
🎯 Objectives
By the end of this unit you will be able to:
• Tell the difference between descriptive and narrative writing and know when to use each.
• Use vivid adjectives, the five senses and figurative language to describe people, places and things.
• Organise a story around a clear sequence of events using the past tenses and time connectors.
• Combine description and narration in a single, coherent paragraph.

🔍 Warm-up
Read these two sentences.
1) "The old house stood at the end of a narrow, foggy street; its broken windows stared like tired eyes."
2) "Last night, I opened the door slowly, walked into the dark hall and heard a strange noise upstairs."
The first sentence paints a picture — it describes. The second one tells us what happened, step by step — it narrates. Good writing very often mixes the two: it shows a scene and then makes something happen inside it. In this unit you will learn how each type works and how to blend them smoothly.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Section 1 — Descriptive writing
📘 Rules
Descriptive writing helps the reader see, hear, smell, taste and feel what you are describing.
• Use precise adjectives: "a huge, ancient oak tree" is stronger than "a big tree".
• Appeal to the five senses: sight, sound, smell, taste and touch.
• Use similes ("as white as snow") and metaphors ("the sky was a grey blanket").
• Follow a logical order in space: near to far, left to right, or top to bottom.
• Descriptive writing usually uses the present simple for general descriptions, or the past simple when the description is inside a story.

✏️ Examples
Weak: "The garden was nice. There were flowers."
Strong: "The small garden was bursting with colour. Red roses climbed the old stone wall, and the sweet smell of jasmine filled the warm evening air."
Notice the precise adjectives (small, red, old, stone, sweet, warm), the appeal to smell, and the clear picture the reader can imagine.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Section 2 — Narrative writing
📘 Rules
Narrative writing tells a story. A good narrative has:
• A setting (where and when it happens).
• Characters (who is involved).
• A plot with a beginning, a problem or climax, and an ending.
• A clear sequence of events told mostly in the past simple, with the past continuous for background actions ("While I was walking, ...") and the past perfect for earlier events ("When we arrived, the train had already left").
• Time connectors: first, then, after that, suddenly, meanwhile, finally.

✏️ Example
"Last summer, we decided to climb Mount Boukornine. First, we packed our bags and set off early. While we were climbing, the weather suddenly changed. Dark clouds gathered and it began to rain. We had not brought our raincoats, so we sheltered under a rock. Finally, the sun came out again and we reached the top, tired but proud."
Notice the time connectors, the past simple for the main events, the past continuous ("were climbing") and the past perfect ("had not brought").

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Section 3 — Combining description and narration
📘 Rules
Strong paragraphs usually mix the two techniques: you describe the setting and the characters, then narrate the events.
• Open with description to set the scene.
• Move into narration to tell what happened.
• Keep one consistent tense (usually the past) throughout the story.

✏️ Example
"The beach was quiet and golden in the early morning light. A gentle breeze carried the salty smell of the sea. (description) Suddenly, a little boy ran towards the water, laughing loudly. He picked up a shiny shell and showed it to his mother. They smiled and walked slowly along the shore. (narration)"

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🛠️ Method — writing a descriptive-narrative paragraph
1. Brainstorm: jot down the place, the people and the main event.
2. Plan the order: description first to set the scene, then the sequence of events.
3. Draft: write a topic sentence, then 8-12 sentences using adjectives, the senses and time connectors.
4. Revise: check your tenses (past simple, past continuous, past perfect); replace weak words with vivid ones; add a simile.
5. Edit: check spelling, punctuation and paragraph indentation.

⚠️ Common mistakes
• Mixing tenses (writing "walked" and then "walk" in the same story).
• Using vague words (nice, good, thing, stuff) instead of precise ones.
• Listing adjectives with no order or purpose.
• Forgetting time connectors, so the events feel disconnected.
• "Telling" instead of "showing": "It was scary" is weaker than "My hands were shaking and my heart was pounding."

⭐ Recap
Descriptive writing paints a picture using precise adjectives and the five senses. Narrative writing tells a story in a clear sequence using the past tenses and time connectors. The best writing combines the two: describe the scene, then make something happen in it. Always keep your tenses consistent, choose vivid words, and show rather than tell.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📘 Useful language bank
• Adjectives for people: cheerful, generous, curious, brave, gentle, stubborn, elegant.
• Adjectives for places: crowded, peaceful, gloomy, spacious, ancient, lively, deserted.
• Sense words: glowing, whispering, fragrant, bitter, rough, freezing, dazzling.
• Time connectors: first, next, then, after a while, suddenly, meanwhile, at last, finally.
• Useful similes: as busy as a bee, as light as a feather, as cold as ice, as quiet as a mouse.

Keep this bank close when you draft: one strong adjective and one time connector in each sentence will instantly make your paragraph richer and clearer.

enonce.question: Write five descriptive sentences about your school. Use at least four different adjectives and appeal to at least two senses.
Rewrite these weak sentences to make them more descriptive: (a) The dog was big. (b) The food was good. (c) The weather was bad.

Read the short text and say which sentences are DESCRIPTIVE and which are NARRATIVE: (1) The lake was calm and silver under the moon. (2) Suddenly, a boy jumped into the water. (3) The trees around it were tall and dark. (4) He swam quickly to the other side.
Write a short descriptive paragraph (5-6 sentences) about your favorite room in your house. Use at least 3 adjectives to describe it.
Write a narrative paragraph (8-10 sentences) about a school trip. Use the past simple, at least one past continuous, and four time connectors.
Join each pair of sentences using the past continuous or the past perfect: (a) I was doing my homework. The lights went off. (b) The film started. We arrived at the cinema.
Write a descriptive paragraph (6-8 sentences) about a member of your family. Use adjectives, the senses, and at least one simile.
Write a narrative paragraph (8-10 sentences) about a memorable day you had with your family. Use past simple verbs and time expressions like 'last weekend', 'yesterday', 'in the morning'.
Write a descriptive-narrative paragraph (10-12 sentences) about a stormy night you remember. Describe the setting, then narrate what happened. Keep your tenses consistent.
Write a short story (10-12 sentences) that teaches a lesson (a moral). Combine description and narration, and end with the moral in one sentence.
Continue this story in 8-10 sentences, keeping the past tense and adding description and time connectors: 'When I opened the old wooden box in the attic, I could not believe my eyes...'

Write a descriptive and narrative paragraph (10-12 sentences) combining description and narration. Describe your best friend and narrate a time when you helped each other. Use adjectives, past simple verbs, and time expressions.
